intended_object: The canonical group isomorphism D_n(R) ≅ Hom_{Spec K}(Spec R, D_n). It identifies the group of invertible diagonal n×n matrices over a K-algebra R with the R-valued points of the diagonal group scheme D_n = Spec(O(GL_n)/(x_ij, i≠j)) over Spec K. This comes from the docstring, the module doc (Milne §2.9) and how the library uses it, in `diagonalGroupPointsIso`.
explanation:
The body composes two group isomorphisms:
- `diagonalGroupMulEquivAlgHom` sends an invertible diagonal matrix s to the K-algebra map O(D_n) → R obtained by evaluating the GL coordinate ring at s. This map factors through the quotient by the off-diagonal entries, since those entries of s are 0. The inverse sends a K-algebra map f to the matrix (f(x_ij)). The equivalence is multiplicative for the convolution product on algebra maps.
- Mathlib's `Spec.mapMulEquiv` identifies algebra maps out of a Hopf algebra with morphisms of affine schemes over Spec K, with their group structure.

Together these give exactly the standard functor-of-points identification of the group scheme D_n with the diagonal subgroup of GL_n(R).

The generality is natural: K is any commutative ring, n any finite index type with decidable equality, and R any commutative K-algebra. The single universe level is the usual Mathlib constraint for Spec and CommRingCat.

Mathlib has no diagonal (split torus) group scheme or comparable points isomorphism. `Spec.mapMulEquiv` is only the general ingredient, so there is no counterpart.
